edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Εἰ γὰρ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα μέ τινες ἠθέλησαν πλανῆσαι, ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα οὐ πλανᾶται ἀπὸ θεοῦ ὄν. οἶδεν γάρ, πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει, καὶ τὰ κρυπτὰ ἐλέγχει. ἐκραύγασα μεταξὺ ὤν, ἐλάλουν μεγάλῃ φωνῇ, θεοῦ φωνῇ: Τῷ ἐπισκοπῳ προσέχετε καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καὶ διακόνοις. [2] οἱ δὲ ὑποπτεύσαντές με ὡς προειδότα τὸν μερισμόν τινων λέγειν ταῦτα: μάρτυς δέ μοι, ἐν ᾧ δέδεμαι, ὅτι ἀπὸ σαρκὸς ἀνθρωπίνης οὐκ ἔγνων. τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ἐκήρυσσεν λέγον τάδε: Χωρὶς τοῦ ἐπισκόπου μηδὲν ποιεῖτε, τὴν σάρκα ὑμῶν ὡς ναὸν θεοῦ τηρεῖτε, τὴν ἕνωσιν ἀγαπᾶτε, τοὺς μερισμοὺς φεύγετε, μιμηταὶ γίνεσθε Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: For even if some wished to deceive me according to the flesh, yet the Spirit is not deceived, being from God. For it knows where it comes from and where it goes, and it exposes the hidden things. I cried out when I was among you; I was speaking with a loud voice, with God's voice: Pay attention to the bishop and to the presbytery and deacons. But some suspected me of saying these things because I knew in advance about the division of certain people. But he in whom I am bound is my witness that I did not learn it from human flesh. The Spirit was proclaiming, saying this: Do nothing without the bishop; keep your flesh as a temple of God; love unity; flee divisions; become imitators of Jesus Christ, as he also is of his Father.
pass_b_english: Some may have wanted to deceive me in the flesh. But the Spirit is not deceived, for it comes from God. It knows where it comes from and where it is going (John 3:8), and it lays bare what is hidden. While I was with you I cried out. I spoke with a loud voice, God's own voice: "Pay attention to the bishop, to the presbytery, and to the deacons."

Some suspected I said this because I already knew that certain people were causing division. But the One in whom I am bound is my witness: I did not learn it from any human being. The Spirit was preaching, and this is what it said: "Do nothing without the bishop. Guard your flesh as God's temple. Love unity. Run from divisions. Become imitators of Jesus Christ, as he is of his Father (1 Corinthians 11:1)."

choices.why: Capitalized: the Spirit who speaks through him and 'proclaims' in 7.2. The neuter pronoun 'it' follows the Greek and John 3:8.
Ignatius claims prophetic speech; kept short and strong.

choices.english: I did not learn it from any human being
rejected: I got no intelligence from any man

choices.english: Do nothing ... Guard ... Love ... Run ... Become
choices.why: The Spirit's message is a string of commands; kept as separate short sentences.
rejected: one long list joined by semicolons

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF 'for whose sake I am in bonds' loosens ἐν ᾧ δέδεμαι (in whom I am bound); ANF 'bodies' for σάρκα.

bible_refs.note: μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε καθὼς κἀγὼ Χριστοῦ; same form of the imitation command

notes: 'Keep your flesh as God's temple' may echo 1 Corinthians 3:16-17 or 6:19; not cited inline.
'Lays bare what is hidden' may echo 1 Corinthians 14:24-25; not cited inline.
Whether τὸ πνεῦμα is the Holy Spirit or Ignatius's own spirit is debated; the prophetic frame favors the Holy Spirit.
Source shows 'ἐπισκοπῳ' without accent; reproduced as supplied.

review.notes: Paragraph 1 checked clause by clause. Pass A holds 'For even if some wished to deceive me according to the flesh, yet the Spirit is not deceived, being from God' for 'Εἰ γὰρ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα μέ τινες ἠθέλησαν πλανῆσαι, ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα οὐ πλανᾶται ἀπὸ θεοῦ ὄν,' and 'I did not learn it from human flesh' for 'ἀπὸ σαρκὸς ἀνθρωπίνης οὐκ ἔγνων.' Pass B does not: 'Some may have wanted to deceive me in the flesh' and 'I did not learn it from any human being.' Pass B also adds agency in 'certain people were causing division' against 'τὸν μερισμὸν τινων' and Pass A 'the division of certain people.' Commands from 'Χωρὶς τοῦ ἐπισκόπου μηδὲν ποιεῖτε' through 'μιμηταὶ γίνεσθε Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ' match in both. Title 'The Spirit Cried Out' names a thought, not a locus.
reasons: Pass B 'Some may have wanted to deceive me in the flesh' drops the concessive and replaces the aorist indicative in 'Εἰ γὰρ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα μέ τινες ἠθέλησαν πλανῆσαι' (Pass A: 'For even if some wished to deceive me according to the flesh') with epistemic 'may have wanted.'

Pass B 'I did not learn it from any human being' omits σάρξ from 'ἀπὸ σαρκὸς ἀνθρωπίνης οὐκ ἔγνων,' which Pass A keeps as 'I did not learn it from human flesh,' flattening the flesh/Spirit distinction.

Pass B 'because I already knew that certain people were causing division' adds the act of causing, absent from 'ὡς προειδότα τὸν μερισμὸν τινων λέγειν ταῦτα' and from Pass A 'because I knew in advance about the division of certain people.'

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both contain wrong scripture citations: Pass A lacks the required John 3:8 citation despite the lemmas and choices and notes indicating it should be added, and Pass B incorrectly attributes the imitation formula to 1 Corinthians 11:1 when the source clearly parallels Ignatius Philadelphians 7.2 with 1 Corinthians 4:16 (as per standard patristic scholarship and the imitation formula 'μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε καθὼς κἀγὼ Χριστοῦ' which is closer to 1 Corinthians 4:16 than 11:1). The Greek text does not contain any wording matching 1 Corinthians 11:1, and the citation in Pass B is therefore false.
reasons: Pass A omits the required inline citation for John 3:8 despite the lemma for πνεῦμα and the notes indicating it should be added; the Greek phrase 'πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει' is a clear allusion to John 3:8 and requires an added citation per rules.

Pass B falsely cites 1 Corinthians 11:1 for the imitation formula; the Greek 'μιμηταὶ γίνεσθε Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ' parallels Ignatius' known use of 1 Corinthians 4:16 elsewhere (e.g., Philadelphians 7.2 mirrors 1 Corinthians 4:16's 'μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε'), and 1 Corinthians 11:1 has a different grammatical structure ('μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε, καθὼς κἀγὼ Χριστοῦ'); the citation in Pass B is therefore wrong and not supported by the Greek.
